items.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: The guy who manages Jackson — Al Jackson — he and the late Jack the Rapper of Atlanta, Georgia.

ctx.x: Like you were talking about before.

Even the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band. Starting in the year 2000, Al may not tell you but I’m telling you because I know, I’ve got proof. They would not have gotten to Europe and Sweden and Denmark without me being in the band from 2001 to now. Even now I’m supposed to go on tour with them, I can’t go because I’m going to be in France. The guy is really upset. Because they didn’t book the tour soon enough for me to be with © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

them. But I walk on tables, I walk on the bar, and still play — do whatever it took to get the band back. They got a lot of repeat business. I wish I didn’t have to tell you this myself. Because it’s unknown. In fact, one time I had to take a plane every day to get back to the Harlem Jazz and Blues Band, because I was double booked.
